## What you will make

This tutorial uses the `vowel` dataset to create a grouped PCA analysis with `dp_pca()`. One fitted object supplies five displays:

<style>
.dppca-display-table table { width: 100%; table-layout: fixed; }
.dppca-display-table colgroup col:nth-child(1) { width: 15% !important; }
.dppca-display-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) { width: 40% !important; }
.dppca-display-table colgroup col:nth-child(3) { width: 45% !important; }
</style>

::: {.dppca-display-table}
| Display | What it shows | A useful question |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Scree/PVE | Estimated variation along the retained PC directions | How is the estimated variation distributed across components? |
| Score | A private histogram or synthetic points on two PC axes | How do the vowel groups overlap in this view? |
| Loading | Coefficients of the PC direction vectors | Which acoustic features contribute to the displayed directions? |
| Variable | Correlation-style variable coordinates | How strongly do the retained components represent each feature? |
| Biplot | Score points and variable arrows together | How do the displayed observations and features relate geometrically? |
:::


This tutorial focuses on **R arguments, stored results, and plots**. 
For the mathematics underlying all five displays, see [DP PCA Visualization Methodology](method-dp-visualization.html). 
The individual estimation mechanisms are covered by [DP Directions Methodology](method-dp-loading.html), [DP Scree Methodology](method-dp-scree.html), and
[DP Score Methodology](method-dp-score.html). For general setup and input requirements, see [Getting Started](tutorials-getting-started.html).

## 1. Load the vowel data

```{r pca-data}
library(dppca)
data("vowel", package = "dppca")
X <- vowel

dim(X)
names(X)
```

`vowel` contains **990 observations and 14 columns**. For more details, see the documentation for [`vowel`](../reference/vowel.html).

<style>
.dp-pca-table table { width: 100%; table-layout: fixed; }
.dp-pca-table colgroup col:nth-child(1) { width: 20% !important; }
.dp-pca-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) { width: 40% !important; }
.dp-pca-table colgroup col:nth-child(3) { width: 40% !important; }
</style>

::: {.dp-pca-table}
| Columns | Contents | Role in this tutorial |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `F0`--`F9` | Ten numeric acoustic features | PCA variables |
| `Split` | Training/test membership | Excluded categorical column |
| `Speaker` | Speaker identity, with 15 levels | Excluded categorical column |
| `Sex` | Speaker sex | Excluded categorical column |
| `Class` | Vowel category, with 11 levels | Group label, excluded from PCA variables |
::: 


Keep `X` as a data frame. `dp_pca()` retains numeric features and reports the excluded columns. 
There is no need to manually remove the four categorical columns or convert them to numbers. 


## 2. Create the privacy allocation

Integrated PCA needs three components: **loading**, **scree**, and **score**.
When `split` is omitted, `dp_pca()` gives each stage one third of the total epsilon and delta:

```{r pca-privacy}
privacy <- privacy_control(eps = 10, delta = 1e-4)
privacy$total
privacy$budgets
```

## 3. Fit DP PCA analysis

In `dp_pca()`, exactly one method must be selected for each estimation step:

- **Scree estimation:** One of `"clipped"`, `"pmwm"`, or `"huber"`. See the [DP Scree Plot Tutorial](tutorials-scree-plots.html) for details.
- **Score histogram estimation:** One of `"add"` or `"sparse"`. See the [DP Score Plot Tutorial](tutorials-score-plots.html) for details.

### Main arguments of `dp_pca()`

::: {.dppca-table}
| Argument | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `X` | Input data matrix or data frame with at least two numeric variables. Non-numeric columns are excluded from the PCA features. |
| `privacy` | Privacy settings from `privacy_control()`, allocated to loading, scree, and score estimation. |
| `scree` | Required list specifying `k`, `method`, `control`, and optionally `mono`. Defaults within the list are `k = NULL` (all components), `method = "clipped"`, and `mono = TRUE`; a method-specific `control` is required. |
| `score` | List specifying the private histogram `method` (`"sparse"` or `"add"`) and `bins`. Defaults: `method = "sparse"`, `bins = c(20, 20)`. |
| `axes` | Two distinct PC indices used for the score plot and biplot. Default: `c(1, 2)`. |
| `group` | Optional grouping column name or vector of group labels. The grouping column is excluded from PCA features. Default: `NULL`. |
| `non_private` | Whether to compute and store an ordinary PCA reference for comparison. If `TRUE`, `plot()` automatically displays both ordinary and DP results; if `FALSE`, only DP results are shown. Default: `FALSE`. |
| `V_dp` | Optional previously estimated full private PC direction matrix. When supplied, loading estimation is skipped. Default: `NULL`. |
| `cpp.option` | Whether to use the compiled implementation when estimating private PC directions internally. Default: `TRUE`. |
:::


For detailed explanations of the `scree` and `score` options, including available estimation methods and their tuning parameters, see the [DP Scree Plot Tutorial](tutorials-scree-plots.html) and [DP Score Plot Tutorial](tutorials-score-plots.html), respectively.


The `V_dp` argument allows previously estimated private PC directions to be reused in `dp_score()`. 
For a detailed example, see [Reusing Private PC Directions](tutorials-scree-plots.html#reusing-private-pc-directions) in the DP Scree Plot tutorial.

Estimate four scree components and use PC1 and PC2 for the score grid:

```{r pca-fit}
set.seed(123)
pca_fit <- dp_pca(
  X,
  privacy = privacy,
  scree = list(
    k = 4,
    method = "clipped",
    control = clipped_control(C_clip = 3)
  ),
  score = list(method = "sparse", bins = c(9, 9)),
  axes = c(1, 2),
  group = "Class"
)

pca_fit
```

The fit reports that ten numeric variables are used, that `Split`, `Speaker`, `Sex`, and `Class` are excluded from PCA, and that the grouping variable is `Class`. It also lists the 11 observed vowel groups.

## 4. Inspect the results

The summary reports estimated component importance, the allocated privacy budgets, selected axes, and group information. 

```{r pca-summary}
pca_summary <- summary(pca_fit)
pca_summary
```

| Stored component | Contains |
|:--|:--|
| `pca_fit$directions` | The full 10-by-10 private direction matrix |
| `pca_fit$scree`, `$pve` | Four estimated scree values and their normalized contributions |
| `pca_fit$frame`, `$hist` | The private frame and pooled score histogram |
| `pca_fit$score_groups` | Private histograms for the vowel groups |
| `pca_fit$metadata$privacy$total`, `$budgets` | Total and stage-specific privacy budgets |
| `pca_fit$metadata$group_name`, `$group_levels` | The selected group name and observed group levels |
| `pca_fit$nonprivate` | The optional ordinary-PCA comparison results |

```{r pca-metadata-privacy}
pca_fit$metadata$privacy$total
pca_fit$metadata$privacy$budgets
```

## 5. Create all five displays

The shortest way to draw the five plots from an existing fit is:

```{r pca-default-plot, fig.alt="Result of DP-PCA"}
plot(pca_fit)
```

If fitted with `non_private = TRUE`, it automatically shows the ordinary reference page first, followed by the DP page. 

```{r pca-overview, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(456)
pca_plots <- plot(
  pca_fit,
  display = "all",
  scree = list(
    type = "pve",                # "pve" or "scree"
    plot_control = NULL
  ),
  score = list(
    type = "sample",             # "histogram" (default) or "sample"
    plot_control = NULL
  ),
  loading = list(
    type = "vector",            # "vector" (default), "point", or "heatmap"
    heatmap_components = NULL,
    plot_control = NULL
  ),
  variable = list(
    plot_control = NULL         
  ),
  biplot = list(
    alpha = 0,
    labels = TRUE,
    plot_control = NULL
  ),
  sampling = sampling_control(  # Shared by score and biplot 
    method = "uniform",
    sample_size = NULL,
    bandwidth_scale = NULL
  ),
  center = TRUE,                # Shared by score and biplot 
  variables = 10,               # Shared by loading, variable and biplot 
  base_size = 12
)
```


<style>
.dppca-table table { width: 100%; table-layout: fixed; }
.dppca-table colgroup col:nth-child(1) { width: 15% !important; }
.dppca-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) { width: 85% !important; }
</style>

::: {.dppca-table}

| Argument | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `display` | Selects which of the five PCA plots to display. Default: `"all"`. |
| `sampling` | Controls synthetic point sampling for the score sample plot and biplot. |
| `center` | Applies the same display-centering setting to the score plot and biplot. Default: `TRUE`. |
| `variables` | Selects variables displayed in the loading, variable, and biplot panels. Default: `10`. |
| `base_size` | Sets the base font size. Default: `12`. |
::: 

The `sampling` argument controls how synthetic points are generated from the score histogram. The same sampled points are used in the score sample plot and biplot. See the [DP Score Plot Tutorial](tutorials-score-plots.html) for details.

By default, `variables = 10` selects the 10 variables with the largest Euclidean norms of their private loading coefficients on the two selected PC axes. The same variables are displayed in the loading, variable, and biplot panels, including non-private comparisons. See the [DP Loading Plot Tutorial](tutorials-loading-plots.html) for details on variable selection.


The `center` argument controls whether the DP score and biplot displays are shifted using the privately estimated score-frame midpoint. By default,
`center = TRUE` places the private frame center at the origin and allows the biplot variable arrows to start at $(0,0)$. See [Display Centering](method-dp-score.html#score-display-centering) for details.


For plot appearance, replace `plot_control = NULL` with a suitable control:

- **Scree:** `scree_plot_control(...)`. See the [DP Scree Plot Tutorial](tutorials-scree-plots.html).
- **Score:** `score_plot_control(...)`. See the [DP Score Plot Tutorial](tutorials-score-plots.html).
- **Loading:** `loading_plot_control(...)`. See the [DP Loading Plot Tutorial](tutorials-loading-plots.html).
- **Variable and biplot:** `plot_control = list(...)` for colors, arrow width, label size, and other display settings.
  
  
## 6. Reuse and export the results

The return value of `plot(pca_fit)` is a list, not a special plot class.

| Component | Contains |
|:--|:--|
| `pca_plots$private$plots` | Named ggplot panels |
| `pca_plots$private$page` | The assembled page grob |
| `pca_plots$private$sampled_points` | Generated points before display centering and biplot scaling |
| `pca_plots$private$biplot` | Biplot coordinate and scaling metadata |
| `pca_plots$nonprivate` | The corresponding ordinary display components, when shown |


```{r pca-save, eval=FALSE}
# One figure
ggplot2::ggsave(
  "vowel-private-biplot.png",
  plot = pca_plots$private$plots$biplot,
  width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300
)

# One complete saved page
grDevices::pdf("vowel-private-pca.pdf", width = 12, height = 8.5)
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(pca_plots$private$page)
grDevices::dev.off()

# The fit can be saved separately for a later R session.
saveRDS(pca_fit, "vowel-pca-fit.rds")
```


For complete argument descriptions, see `?dp_pca`, `?plot.dp_pca`, and `?sampling_control`.
